clue.text: Distress call about British Conservative — a tale of woe

indicators.note: the distress signal goes round the next piece, so 'about' asks for a container here

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An emergency call concerning a British Conservative politician turns out to be a sad story.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-luck story told to win sympathy is a tale of woe, the idiom's exact meaning.

clue.text: Pressure generated when schoolteacher rejects note

indicators.note: the teacher turning away something means those letters are dropped from her title

parts.note: a mistress is an old-fashioned word for a female schoolteacher
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A teacher snubbing a note causes tension in the staffroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress and pressure are synonyms, whether physical force or mental strain.

clue.text: Home supporter first to get hit over the head

indicators.note: 'first' places the supporter ahead of the word for home in the answer

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means at home

explanation.surface: A home fan is the first to be struck on the head in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home supporter' reads as a football fan; 'first' puts the undergarment ahead of the home word. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To brain someone is the informal verb for striking them hard on the head.

clue.text: Twice as much time's taken with old pen

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a fold is a pen for sheep

explanation.surface: Something takes double the time when written with an old pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' is just a link; 'pen' is the sheep enclosure, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Twofold means double, so a twofold quantity is twice as much.

clue.text: Lead for building material? Steel for it, rather

parts.note: a rein is a lead used to guide a horse
taken as written
cement is a building material

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether lead suits a building material and is told steel would be better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal, but it is a rein. The definition runs on from the surface: steel, rather than lead, is what strengthens concrete.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel rods set in concrete are its strengthening, so steel serves as the building material's support.

clue.text: Black Sea port where seas do get rough

indicators.note: seas becoming rough are churned up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A harbour on the Black Sea where the water often turns stormy.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Ukrainian port on the Black Sea coast.

clue.text: Academic piece of work you wouldn't want to hear

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: A scholar's assignment is so dull nobody wants to listen to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said as a warning that the full story is something the listener would rather not learn.

clue.text: The significance of a text means it's wrenched out of chapter

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the abbreviation, so 'out of' sets them around it
words wrenched are twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A text's meaning gets distorted when a quotation is torn from its chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrenched' makes SEMANTIS, and 'out of' sets those letters around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the study of meaning, so it covers what a text signifies.

clue.text: Leander swimming to unknown island

indicators.note: swimming suggests movement in the water, so these letters are swirled into a new order

parts.note: Y is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Leander swims off towards an unnamed island.
explanation.walkthrough: In legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly; 'swimming' rearranges his name into ALDERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney is one of the Channel Islands, a specific example of an island.

clue.text: Thinking son should go where daughter is in studying at University

indicators.note: the son is to take the place where the daughter stands, so one replaces the other

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thoughtful family decides the son should go to the university where his sister is studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' is only linking: D stands in the word for studying, and SON replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the process of thinking things through logically.

clue.text: Comprehend what art thieves can do

definitions.meaning: to understand a situation, as in the informal idiom
a thief in a gallery can literally take a painting

explanation.surface: Understanding what art thieves are capable of.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to understand, and literally describes taking a painting away.

clue.text: Wanderer not sane, surely?

parts.note: no is a word of negation
the doubting question mark turns sane into its opposite, a word for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone who roams endlessly can hardly be in their right mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals ironic doubt: 'sane, surely?' means the opposite, so it gives MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is someone who roams from place to place with no fixed home.

clue.text: Order player to leave celebration

definitions.meaning: a referee may dismiss a footballer from the field
a farewell party is given for someone departing

explanation.surface: A player is dismissed from the field in the middle of a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To send off is a referee's dismissal; a send-off is a farewell party.

clue.text: Comfortable shoe wanted for coach

definitions.meaning: a soft sports shoe, the British word for a sneaker

explanation.surface: A comfortable shoe is wanted for the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted for' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is both a British sports shoe and a person who coaches.

clue.text: Drug knocking out drunken thief before having an operation

indicators.note: knocking something out of shape scatters it, so all these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A thief is knocked out by drugs before undergoing surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' looks like the anagram signal but is part of what gets rearranged; 'knocking out' is the signal. 'before' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under the knife is the idiom for undergoing surgery.

clue.text: Name six in Leeds team not wanted

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the team's name

parts.note: Leeds United is the English football club
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six players are named in the Leeds side but are not welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninvited was not asked, so their presence is not wanted.

clue.text: Badly wants to live — there's an outside chance

parts.note: to long for something is to want it badly
a live wire is a hot one, carrying current

explanation.surface: Someone desperate to stay alive has only a slim hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' is the electrical sense, not survival. 'there's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is a venture with little chance of success.

clue.text: Find bearings to join specific train

parts.note: to orient oneself is to work out one's position
express can mean explicit or specific, as in an express purpose

explanation.surface: Someone works out their direction so they can catch a particular train.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient Express is a famous long-distance luxury train.

clue.text: Short letter not taken out of the box

indicators.note: the negation takes in the television, holding it within

parts.note: taken as written
the box is slang for the television, as is the tele

explanation.surface: A brief letter is left unopened in its box.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet for writing a brief message.

clue.text: Descriptive term needs concise expression in English and French

indicators.note: the word for conciseness sits within the other two pieces

parts.note: et is the French word for 'and'
pith is terse, forceful expression

explanation.surface: A descriptive phrase must be crisp whether in English or French.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a word or phrase describing a person's quality.

clue.text: Primarily, a government establishment newly constituted, yes?

definitions.text: Primarily, a government establishment newly constituted, yes?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a new government body has just been set up.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a government body, the whole clue's picture of a new establishment.

clue.text: Yielded to pressure about wildly excessive dance

indicators.note: the word for yielded goes round the next piece

parts.note: to give is to yield under pressure
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: Someone gives in to pressure to perform an extravagant dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gavotte is an old French dance of moderate tempo.

clue.text: Chat with friend about wife that's little good

indicators.note: the friend goes round the next piece

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Gossiping with a pal about how little use one's wife is.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so 'china' is a friend. 'with' and 'that's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal British word for a chat.

clue.text: Wide aperture is undamaged

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
a hole is an opening

explanation.surface: A wide opening means the thing is intact.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole means intact or in one piece, so undamaged.

clue.text: Letter transmitted offering accommodation

definitions.meaning: the radio code word for H in the NATO alphabet
a place providing rooms for guests

explanation.surface: A letter sent offering a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel is the radio code word for H and a place providing rooms.

clue.text: As Spooner might have described Arnhem landing?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two parts trade starts

parts.note: Arnhem is a town in the Netherlands
Arnhem is a town in the Netherlands

explanation.surface: How the reverend might have described the Arnhem airborne landing of 1944.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnhem is a Dutch town; swapping the opening sounds gives 'touch down'.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchdown is the moment an aircraft lands.

clue.text: Gallery houses what's extremely old up to the present day

indicators.note: the gallery holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery

indicators.note: extremely asks for the letters at the extremes, first and last

explanation.surface: A gallery displays very old works right up to modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: To date is the idiom meaning so far, until now.

clue.text: Like tough skin to be covered in suds around end of bathtime

indicators.note: the soapy word wraps around the final letter

parts.note: lathery means covered in soapy foam

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone is lathered in soap as bath time comes to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery means tough and hard, like old leather.
